scope.method: Static source/test inspection plus Python AST/text checks; no Cargo, build, QEMU, source edits, deployment or git mutations. Only this new JSON artifact is written.
limitations: Not a full allocator, boot-memory or portable-core audit.
Parent-reported builds and 257 passed / 2 ignored are context only, not independently rerun or full acceptance.
Other agents edited/formatted files during review; hashes below identify the post-format snapshot, not an acceptance source freeze.

positive_observations.result: Const-initialized FILESYSTEM, DESCRIPTORS, SYSTEM and disk backend avoid large by-value metadata on boot stack. One boot/main-loop owner retains exclusive borrows; no extra SYSTEM raw borrow after mount observed. This relies on documented single-entry/single-CPU/no-ISR-access invariants.

Bounded full-byte SHA-256 checks independent compiled digest before parse/publication. Immutable owned module copy remains alive across verify/build; ArchiveFs copies payload and retains no source slices.

Fallible parser/node/payload reservations stage an owned replacement; early errors drop staged buffers and preserve previous generation. No frame/VGA guard spans these call sites. Successful replacement drops previous owned Vecs in main context, not under a frame guard. Two parser indexes coexist during build (verify index and reparse index), in addition to input copy and old/new snapshots; account all peak allocations.

Bindings and every canonical prefixed path are staged before RAM mountpoint work. Production has no fallible operation after successful mountpoint resolution. File/nonempty-directory collisions reject without publication; failure fixture rolls back only a directory created by that transaction.

positive_observations.evidence: src/fs/mounted.rs:52-73 and Vfs methods; src/fs/archive.rs:326-352; src/fd.rs:375-408,428-433
positive_observations.result: Disjoint bounded RAM/disk/system slot ranges, generation validation and no system detach/rebuild capability are sound by inspection. All direct system mutators, including old RAM mountpoint write/replace/truncate routes, deny writes. Existing FdTable checks rights before backend writes and dup only attenuates. Disk initialization remains independently gated by accepted inventory and test-owned media.

findings.title: Built but unpublished static ArchiveFs payload is retained after mount refusal
findings.detail: try_build commits allocated nodes/payload into static SYSTEM before mount_system. A collision, prefixed-path error, RAM node exhaustion or fixture mount failure returns only FsError; the exclusive static borrow is consumed and the error arm merely logs. No Drop/reset of SYSTEM releases its owned buffers. Unlike accepted boot-module physical pins (explicitly permanent), this is an unreachable heap snapshot that remains allocated throughout recovery. With a larger reviewed system image or constrained heap this unnecessarily reduces recovery headroom. No dangling-reference/UB was identified; this is resource rollback, not a trust bypass.
findings.requested_change: Define failure ownership explicitly: return the unpublished archive borrow on attachment error, or use a boot-only staged attach API that lets caller reset/drop the unpublished snapshot safely without manufacturing a second alias. Test heap live allocations after successful build followed by each failed mount.
findings.verification: Static lifetime and destructor analysis; no allocator instrumentation run.

findings.title: Negative guest cases accept the wrong recovery class and never prove publication was absent
findings.detail: All non-trusted cases accept the same REJECTION_ALTS, including absent-module and rejected-boot-inventory markers. Thus mount-collision, mount-failure and allocation-refusal can pass after copy/digest/metadata rejection without ever reaching the targeted operation. recovery_shell only exercises unrelated RAMFS files; it does not assert /system absent, preserve the collision file, inspect publication state, or forbid a later trusted marker. Existing marker test intentionally supplies the absent marker for every negative case, encoding this false-positive oracle.
findings.requested_change: Specify exact per-case outcome/error groups and relevant storage-gate state; require publication-refused marker for fixture cases and prove targeted path reached, /system absent when owned by the transaction, preexisting collision identity/content unchanged, and no trusted publication marker. Add host tests rejecting an absent/wrong-class transcript for each targeted scenario.

findings.title: Mounted system allocations and routing metadata have no integrated accounting route
findings.detail: MountedFs::stats includes RAM and optional disk only, never system.stats or system_bindings. Keeping inherited RAMFS quota/baseline semantics separate is reasonable, but there is no separate system diagnostic exposed here either. The namespace can therefore own archive payload/node allocations while integrated FS diagnostics omit them, and final guest diagnostics parse only total/free frames, not heap live/peak or system capacities. This cannot substantiate exact resource accounting or partial-construction cleanup.
findings.requested_change: Keep RAMFS quota accounting separate; expose bounded system payload/node/routing/peak accounting explicitly and test it. Include input copy and two live parser indexes in peak boot-import bounds; do not count retained module frames as reclaimable.

missing_required_tests.requirement: Host test both attachment orders with real portable RostiBackend plus ArchiveFs, cross-boundary traversal, distinct IDs, writable disk, immutable system and independently preserved failure states. Guest trusted-system plus valid owned RostiFS persistence at both boot paths/RAM sizes.
missing_required_tests.observed_gap: Current system tests instantiate MountedFs<RamFs> without mounting a disk; existing portable-core tests do not attach a system archive. Guest matrix attaches only corrupt media for corrupt-rostifs; that case deliberately clears module presence, so even valid-system/corrupt-disk coexistence is untested.

missing_required_tests.requirement: Through MountedFs+ArchiveFs verify READ/STAT/SEEK, duplicated shared offsets, denied escalation, no-WRITE PermissionDenied, explicit-WRITE backend ReadOnly, unchanged offsets and live-record counts on refusal, forged generation/slot boundaries and continued system reads across disk unmount/remount.
missing_required_tests.observed_gap: Existing system mutator tests call Vfs directly; descriptor coverage is RAMFS/disk-only. Guest read-only commands do not replace the missing capability-mask/dup assertions.

missing_required_tests.requirement: File collision with preserved content, nonempty directory collision, mountpoint node-quota failure, canonical /system-prefix boundary success/failure, second attachment Busy, all bindings unpublished on failure and existing cwd/open/duplicated descriptors preserved.
missing_required_tests.observed_gap: System rollback test covers only injected post-point failure with empty preexisting directory or newly created directory; valid mounts cover basic reads/traversal. No full listed boundary matrix.

missing_required_tests.area: actual allocation failure and partial Drop
missing_required_tests.requirement: Deterministic refusal at copy allocation, verification parser, reparse index, nodes and payload with exact live-allocation/Drop accounting; guest real bounded heap pressure with recovery operations, module pins and storage policy preserved.
missing_required_tests.observed_gap: ArchiveFs refusal tests preserve visible old snapshot; they do not count actual staged buffer deallocation. Mode3 refuses nodes before try_reserve_exact and is not real heap exhaustion. Current guest resource-exhaustion case must not be credited as physical allocator exhaustion.

missing_required_tests.requirement: Each distinct recovery class at ELF/GRUB 128/512 must prove target rejection, no partial /system publication, RAMFS create/read/delete, OOM handling, keyboard/VGA/continued dispatch, explicit persistent-storage policy, and hash each attached no-write owned image before/after each refusal path.
missing_required_tests.observed_gap: Current matrix uses no disk for most refusal cases, hashes a single corrupt image only across the aggregate, performs no bounded OOM workload in recovery_shell, and reboots after a digest failure rather than a partial construction/publication failure. Retained real-GRUB trusted positive probes are valuable but not this complete acceptance matrix.

closed_during_review.title: Production checks do not attest absence of the initramfs fixture in the actual ELF being packaged
closed_during_review.detail: verify_production now lists initramfs-failure-test in forbidden metadata features, but cargo metadata with default arguments describes default resolution rather than features of an existing target/debug/kernel. Its binary check excludes only the paging-fault text. The ISO packager likewise rejects only paging-fault text. A previously built initramfs-failure-test ELF can therefore pass these binary/packaging checks, retaining externally writable INITRAMFS_TEST_MODE and refusal/collision routes. The acceptance runner default rebuild and fixture/production hash inequality help its normal path but do not establish fixture absence from an independently supplied/stale ELF.
closed_during_review.requested_change: Reject INITRAMFS_TEST_MODE (or a dedicated unambiguous fixture marker) in the actual ELF before production verification and packaging; retain a host-only mocked test that default cargo metadata plus a fixture ELF fails without launching QEMU/Cargo.
closed_during_review.verification: Static control-flow inspection; did not execute packager or Cargo.
closed_during_review.resolution: verify_production.artifact_policy_checks now rejects INITRAMFS_TEST_MODE in exact payload; ISO main invokes the shared check before packaging.

closed_during_review.title: Trusted ls oracle omits the directory slash emitted by the real shell
closed_during_review.detail: trusted_shell expects ls /system to equal README.txt followed by docs, both before and after write denials. fs_commands appends / to directory names, and exact compares output after trimming only newline characters. A correct mount emits docs/ and this trusted workload fails before completing its read-only checks.
closed_during_review.requested_change: Expect README.txt\ndocs/ and retain a host-only contract using actual shell output conventions rather than a mocked-out trusted_shell.
closed_during_review.resolution: trusted_shell now expects docs/ in both ls assertions.
